seen.where: Zeeuws Archief toegang 72 (J. van den Warck), inv. 9, 23 scans in the archieven.nl viewer (https://www.archieven.nl/nl/search-modonly?mivast=239&mizig=210&miadt=239&micode=72&miview=inv2, section 3); exhibition description at toegang 202.90 no. 4.
seen.extent: Scans 2-16 hold a stack of letters of 1585, some headed Duplicate or Copia, mixing clear openings and closings with long numeric cipher passages; scans 18-20 and 21-23 are clear Latin and other clear text. Wrapper (scan 1) is headed 'Onderscheidene Brieven in Cijffer, en Sleutel 1568, 76 & 1585'.
seen.cipher: Numeric cipher mixed with clear text, seen zoomed on scans 3 and 13. Scan 13 carries letter-by-letter interlinear decipherment above the numbers. The wrapper's pencil note (as far as I can read it) counts six letters of Brabant to the States General 'met twee ontcijferingen', plus keys of decipherment.

prior_art.decode: known.py on 202.90, Warck and Antwerpen 1585 (harvested DECODE dump included): only this lead's own rows, no DECODE record.
prior_art.tomokiyo: General searches naming Antwerp 1585, the magistrates and the States General surfaced no Cryptiana page; the site was not opened directly.
prior_art.lasry: Searches surfaced no Lasry paper on the Van den Warck letters of 1585; GL.htm was not opened.
prior_art.edition: Zeeuws Archief inventory and 2005 exhibition catalogue describe the pack without text; no printed edition of these cipher letters found. The Marnix correspondence edition (1585-98) was not opened and concerns Marnix's own letters.
prior_art.literature: Searches on the siege of Antwerp and Marnix as cryptographer found background only, nothing on these letters. The decipherment on record is the one on the leaves.

1947.key_check: No key was tested. The wrapper names a 'Sleutel' and keys of decipherment; I saw no key table in the 23 scans of inv. 9, so it is either in unscanned inv. 9a or was not recognised at this resolution.
1947.key_in_volume: Wrapper of inv. 9 says 'en Sleutel'; the key leaf was not identified in the scans, possibly in inv. 9a (no scans offered), not tested.
1947.duplicates: known.py on 202.90, Warck, Antwerpen 1585: only this lead and its sweep row. Correction for the lead: senders are the city government of Antwerp and the States of Zeeland, addressees the States General and the States of Brabant at Delft.
1947.closed: Contemporary decipherment is on the leaf: interlinear letters over the numbers on inv. 72/9 scan 13, and the wrapper note records two deciphered letters. The other cipher letters of 1585 in the stack showed no interlinear text at the resolution I viewed (not read leaf by leaf), and could be split into a new lead with the wrapper's keys.

seen.where: Groninger Archieven 2100, no. 1462.491, 5 scans in the viewer via https://hdl.handle.net/21.12105/27567B9B13A345F7B9DCA85E70EA5AF6
seen.extent: Scan 1 Verdugo's letter, clear Dutch with about five lines of cipher; scan 3 Van den Berg's letter, about eighteen lines of cipher between clear German openings and closings, 'Datum Dennekam den 17 Junij 94'; scan 5 a full clear text of Van den Berg's letter; scans 2 and 4 versos and address.
seen.cipher: Letter-and-symbol substitution written continuously, seen zoomed on scan 1 and at page size on scan 3. Scan 5 runs in clear through the place where scan 3 is in cipher, with the same closing and date, and the archive calls it a transcription of Van den Berg's letter.

prior_art.decode: known.py on 1462.491, Verdugo, Denekamp, Herman van den Berg (harvested DECODE dump included): only this lead and an unrelated mention in targets/casimir1618.
prior_art.tomokiyo: General searches naming Verdugo, Van den Berg and the Groningen siege of 1594 surfaced no Cryptiana page; the site was not opened directly.
prior_art.lasry: The same searches returned HistoCrypt papers on other documents, none on Verdugo 1594; GL.htm was not opened.

1948.key_check: No key tested and none in the item. Scan 3 against scan 5 gives a long crib for the cipher, which looks usable for Verdugo's passage on scan 1 if it is the same system (not tested).
1948.duplicates: known.py on the shelfmark and correspondents: no catalogue entry or target holds this document; casimir1618 lists a separate Verdugo alphabet (item 040), not compared.
1948.closed: Van den Berg's cipher letter (scan 3) has a contemporary clear text in the same item (scan 5, the archive's 'transcriptie'). Verdugo's short cipher passage on scan 1 has no decipherment on the leaf or in the item, and is short work with the scan 3/5 crib if the system matches.

seen.where: Nationaal Archief 2.21.008.69 (family Van Hogendorp), inv. 34, https://www.nationaalarchief.nl/onderzoeken/archief/2.21.008.69/invnr/34 ; same text on Archives Portal Europe. The inventory says 'Bekijken: studiezaal', so there are no scans.
seen.extent: One letter among 6 pieces dated 2 Nov 1802 to 9 Aug 1808; length of the cipher is not stated.
seen.cipher: Inventory: 'Inhoud: Brief in cijferschrift van den gezant Van Spaen (1802)', naming the piece itself as a letter in cipher. Leaf not seen, so whether a decipherment is written on it is unknown.

searches.query: Colenbrander Gedenkstukken Spaen (full-text search of the Huygens retroboeken, 118 hits, deel 4 read in the index)
searches.result: Deel 4 band 2 index, p. 781: Spaen van Voorstonde, 'gezant naar Weenen', pp. 158, 672, 674. P. 674 only names him at conferences in The Hague (Feb 1802) and p. 158 reports his Vienna posting in a snippet (p. 672 not opened); the index lists no dispatch of his and no 1802 cipher letter appeared.

searches.query: Dirk van Hogendorp archief 'Sleutels van geheimschrift' OR 'Brief in cijferschrift' Van Spaen 1802 Oostenrijksch Hollandsche schuld ontcijferd
searches.result: Biographies only; a DBNL entry confirms Hogendorp replaced Van Spaen van Voorstonde at Vienna. No decipherment of the 1802 letter.

searches.query: cryptiana Dutch Batavian Republic diplomatic cipher 1802 Van Spaen van Voorstonde Vienna envoy code Lasry Tomokiyo DECODE Dutch legation code deciphered
searches.result: Nothing on this letter. Closest is a study of Willem Six's St Petersburg codebook 1806-10 (dspace.ut.ee), a different legation and period.

searches.query: 'Van Spaen' Bataafsche gezant 1802 Weenen OR Vienna OR Berlijn 'Gedenkstukken' Colenbrander cijfers depeche Oostenrijksche lening Hogendorp
searches.result: A DBNL note on Van Spaen's letters to Van Musschenbroek 1802-17 and a UU entry on G. C. van Spaen as Vienna representative; no cipher text or decipherment.
